status: frozen 2026-09-15 before held-out validation; parameters must not change under this version

device.model: Raspberry Pi Compute Module 3 Plus Rev 1.0 (BCM2835 revision a02100)
device.cpu: 4x ARMv7 Processor rev 4 (Cortex-A53), armv7l userspace, 1200 MHz, performance governor, throttled=0x0
device.background: 10 mods loaded at boot (emplaitress, nb_polyperc, matrix, toolkit, oilcan, nb_rudiments, nb_ansible, nb_jf, nb_crow, doubledecker); Wi-Fi (RT5370) up; idle matron main thread about 2.2% CPU

norns_runtime.note: 14bbeae (emulator pin) plus release-notes and update.sh commits only; stock clock.lua 39b6c3ac..., matron c1c2d5e0...

reference_host.note: reference_host_us, reference_lua_factor and calibration_bias were measured here; the runtime recalibrates on each host

units.lua_targets_us: device median wall time of the probe kernels lua_arith, lua_table, lua_string, lua_calls, lua_memory_access, lua_memory_churn (microseconds)
units.lua_kernel_weights: geometric weights of per-kernel device/host ratios: fixed prior of half memory-bound, half CPU-bound (not fitted)
units.reference_host_us: median fastest-of-nine in-runtime calibration kernel times on the reference host (microseconds); normalises the consistency check
units.reference_lua_factor: weighted in-script device/host ratio on the reference host at which binding costs were fitted
units.calibration_bias: in-script / in-runtime calibrated factor ratio on the reference host
units._call_us: signed device-equivalent microseconds per binding call, replacing host native time (includes correction for over-scaled binding glue)

check.ratio: device median / emulator median of per-repeat medians

unchecked_known_gaps.midi_send_burst_1 / midi_send_burst_16 /: emulator 1.6-4x slower: host wake-up cost after idle is scaled with the Lua work

check.count_tolerance_rationale: Burst counts depend on stall phase relative to ticks; unprofiled local emulator runs already varied by one (native-default-01, 2026-09-15) before the CI run; the initial exact rule was a check design error.
check.kernel_expectation: One Lua factor cannot reproduce every code shape: individual kernels are not expected to match. The weighted geometric mean of device/emulator kernel ratios (the calibrated quantity) must lie within ratio_bounds.

diagnostic_blocks.screen_frame: Screen binding glue is below a microsecond per call, at the resolution of host clock accounting; a GitHub-hosted runner measured 2x fast. Reported, not gating; musical effect is bounded (about 0.15 ms per 128-call frame) and PERF-005 held-out rendering pressure tests it at workload level.

check.calibration_note: Kernel-shape spread against the reference host is diagnostic; the runtime itself refuses hosts whose two calibration passes disagree by more than 10%.

limitations: A single Lua factor blends code shapes: on the reference host pure CPU-bound Lua runs about 1.6x faster than the device and cache-bound table access about 2x slower. Workload conclusions hold where the Lua mix resembles the calibration workloads.
Models Lua-thread execution and MIDI/grid/screen binding cost only; screen rendering thread, JACK/crone audio load, SD storage latency and memory pressure are not modelled.
Timing is observed at the native MIDI boundary in the emulator and at a Lua send wrapper on the device.
Emulator JACK runs the dummy driver at 1024 frames; the device uses ALSA at 128 frames.
Mods loaded on the device are absent from emulator sessions.

frozen.host_calibration: two independent in-runtime kernel passes must agree within 10% (three attempts), fastest-of-nine per kernel
